candidates.explanation: Board clearly owns orchestration and policy, sibling capabilities remain independent, and the page calls the board query. The board depends directly on capability APIs rather than defining board-language ports/adapters, so that criterion is only partial. Authorization is coherent, but unexpected-failure reporting exactly once is not clearly specified; the structured report discussed mainly concerns inaccessible labels.

Board owns the projection and policy, the page uses a board-owned entrypoint, authorization is layered, and a single reporting boundary is explicit. However, board imports published work-item and label use-case operations rather than narrow public server surfaces through board-owned adapters. Those paths are application internals, producing negative violation 2.

Board-owned ports and orchestration are well described, sibling dependencies remain acyclic, and authorization plus once-only reporting are strong. But the concrete foreign surfaces are application port files, which are application internals rather than narrow public server entrypoints. The route also calls a board DAL adapter rather than an explicit board RSC/public surface.

The design has strong board-language ports, narrow capability-owned server surfaces, an acyclic graph, a board RSC surface, layered authorization, and once-only unexpected-failure reporting. Orchestration is reduced to partial because the stated parallel calls conflict with the later requirement to derive referenced label IDs from the work-item result; the label read must be sequenced after that derivation or use a differently defined input.
